principle: Localized electrodeposition without a tank: the workpiece is made cathodic and a hand-held (or fixture-held) insoluble anode wrapped in an absorbent cover (cotton, felt, PermaWrap-class sleeve) is saturated with plating solution and moved over the work surface; deposition occurs only where the wetted swab contacts the part. The constant relative anode-cathode motion thins the diffusion boundary layer drastically, so brush plating tolerates current densities 5-50x higher than still-tank plating and builds thickness fast in the contact zone [FACT: published characteristic of brush plating]. Solutions are more concentrated and more heavily complexed than tank baths so they stay stable in an open, aerated, hand-carried format. In jewelry the same principle at miniature scale is 'pen plating': a small platinum-tipped or graphite pen with a fiber nib, 50-500 ml of solution, and a low-voltage rectifier, used for selective gold accents, two-tone work, and repair of worn spots.

substrates: nickel or nickel-plated steel (standard target surface for gold brush work)
stainless steel (needs brush nickel/Wood's-type activation first)
carbon steel (needs brush Ni undercoat; never brush gold direct onto bare steel)
any conductive surface reachable by the swab
applicability.steel_wire_notes: For the anchor steel-wire jewelry product, brush plating is NOT the production route — it is the REPAIR and ACCENT route. Whole-piece coverage of formed wire rings by hand-swab is slow, uneven, and operator-limited; tank (rack/barrel) plating covers full pieces far cheaper per piece. Where brush earns its place: (1) re-plating worn high spots on returned/stock pieces without stripping the whole item; (2) selective second-color accents (e.g. rose-gold detail on a yellow-gold ring, rhodium tips); (3) plating AFTER forming/assembly on one small zone (solder joint, clasp) that forming damaged — this partially answers the plate-then-form problem: form first, tank-plate, then brush-repair any forming damage on prototypes; (4) plating assembled pieces with stones/components that cannot be immersed. Contact point for the cathode clip must be planned — it leaves an unplated/marked spot, so clip on a hidden zone.
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Same rule as all electro-processes: glass/ceramic houseware cannot be brush plated without a conductive seed layer (silvering, conductive paint, electroless Cu/Ni). On mixed pieces (metal spoon with plastic handle) brush plating is actually the ENABLING route: the metal bowl can be plated selectively without immersing the non-metal handle. Food-contact of pen-plated gold over Ni on cutlery: regulatory status [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check per market].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: Brush/pen gold is realistically a FLASH-to-LIGHT-MICRON tool on jewelry: 0.05-0.5 um typical per application, up to ~1-2 um with patient multiple passes and ampere-hour counting [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high]. Industrial brush plating (SIFCO/Dalic-class, MIL-STD-865 work) builds tens of microns of Ni/Cu/Ag on machine parts, but decorative gold at jewelry cost is almost always kept sub-micron per spot. Heavy-wear classes (2.5-5 um full-coverage) are tank territory; do not sell brush-only coverage as 'micron plating'.

components.name: portable DC rectifier / pen-plating power supply
components.purpose: voltage-controlled DC source, typically 0-15 V (jewelry pen units 2-8 V working range; industrial brush units 0-25 V, 15-150 A); many industrial units integrate an ampere-hour meter for thickness control
components.diy_notes: a bench CC/CV lab PSU (0-30 V, 0-5 A) is fully adequate for jewelry pen work; commercial pen-plating stations add convenience (preset voltages, Ah counter) not capability. Polarity: work = NEGATIVE (cathode), pen = POSITIVE, for deposition; reversed polarity turns the tool into a deplater/electropolisher (also useful).

components.name: anode pen / stylus / brush tool
components.purpose: insoluble anode delivering current through the solution-soaked cover to the contact zone
components.diy_notes: jewelry pens: platinum or platinized-titanium tip with interchangeable fiber/felt nibs; industrial styli: high-purity graphite blocks shaped to the work (graphite is the standard workhorse anode for brush plating [FACT]) or platinized Ti for small tools. DIY: graphite rod (pure, not clay-bonded pencil lead) wrapped in cotton works; NEVER stainless or copper as anode (dissolves contaminants into the gold solution).

components.name: absorbent anode covers/nibs
components.purpose: hold electrolyte, prevent direct anode-cathode short (arcing/burning), define contact footprint
components.diy_notes: cotton batting + cotton tube gauze (industrial standard), felt nibs, or wrapped cotton swab tips; keep dedicated covers per solution — a nib that touched nickel solution poisons the gold solution on next dip.

components.name: cathode contact clip/probe
components.purpose: reliable electrical connection to the workpiece
components.diy_notes: alligator clip with copper jaws on a hidden feature; for tiny pieces, a stainless tweezer probe wired as cathode held by the operator; contact spot will not plate — plan geometry.

components.name: solution cups + drip station
components.purpose: small working volumes (30-500 ml) the pen is re-dipped into; catch tray for drips
components.diy_notes: glass/PP beakers; NEVER dip a used nib back into stock bottles — pour a working aliquot, discard or keep separate; gold solution economy improves dramatically with a dedicated drag-out cup for nib rinsing (gold recovery).

components.name: prep pens/solutions (electroclean + activator)
components.purpose: same pen technique with cleaning and activating solutions ahead of plating — full brush prep chain without tanks
components.diy_notes: commercial pen systems sell electrocleaner and activator solutions used with the same handle at reversed or normal polarity per TDS; DIY minimum = manual degrease + acid activation dip before pen work.

components.name: optional flow/pumped system
components.purpose: industrial brush plating recirculates solution through the anode tool for large-area/high-rate work
components.diy_notes: irrelevant at jewelry scale; only if brush plating machine bores/houseware panels later.

components.name: ventilation + PPE station
components.purpose: open-surface work with (often cyanide-complex) gold solution inches from the operator's hand
components.diy_notes: nitrile gloves mandatory, eye protection, work over a tray, small extractor fan or open-window airflow; keep acids physically separated from any cyanide-type solution [FACT: HCN generation on acid contact with cyanide solutions].

operation_sequence.action: plan the job: define the zone to plate, mask adjacent areas if needed (lacquer/tape platers' masking), choose cathode contact point on a hidden feature
operation_sequence.parameters: masking: platers tape or peelable lacquer
operation_sequence.failure_watch: no plan = solution creep plating areas you didn't want, visible contact-clip mark on a show surface

operation_sequence.action: clean the target zone: degrease (solvent wipe/ultrasonic), then electroclean pen or alkaline wipe, rinse
operation_sequence.failure_watch: skin oils from handling AFTER cleaning are the classic pen-plating adhesion killer — handle with gloves/tweezers from here on

operation_sequence.action: activate: acid activator pen/dip appropriate to the surface (dilute sulfuric/proprietary for Ni; Wood's-type nickel strike pen for stainless)
operation_sequence.failure_watch: passive nickel (sat >1-2 min after activation) = peeling gold; re-activate if delayed

operation_sequence.action: if base is steel/stainless/worn-through: brush-plate nickel undercoat first with the nickel pen solution
operation_sequence.parameters: typically 4-8 V, continuous motion [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: gold direct on steel = immersion deposit + iron contamination of the gold nib/solution

operation_sequence.action: rinse zone, connect work as CATHODE, set rectifier voltage per gold solution TDS, dip nib in gold working aliquot
operation_sequence.parameters: gold pen typical 3-6 V [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high; exact per TDS]; polarity verified
operation_sequence.failure_watch: reversed polarity = you strip/etch instead of plate; too-dry nib = arcing/black burn marks

operation_sequence.action: plate: keep the nib MOVING in constant overlapping strokes with light pressure, re-wetting every few seconds; count time or ampere-hours for thickness
operation_sequence.parameters: constant motion ~5-25 m/min relative speed class (industrial guidance) [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]; flash coverage in 10-30 s, ~0.1 um-class in 1-3 min per small zone [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: stopping in one spot = burn/dark patch; dry-out = streaks and scorch; low voltage = no coverage over Ni (stays white)

operation_sequence.action: rinse immediately (first rinse into a dedicated gold-recovery cup), then clean water rinse, dry soft-cloth/warm air
operation_sequence.failure_watch: dried-on solution = stains/spots; cyanide-type residue left on a wearable item is a safety and corrosion fault

operation_sequence.action: inspect and test: color match vs retained standard under daylight lamp, tape/burnish adhesion check on a test coupon done with the same sequence, thickness by XRF if claiming a class
operation_sequence.failure_watch: pen work drifts with nib wear and solution depletion — re-verify against the standard every batch, not once

solutions.solution_name: gold pen/brush solution, cyanide type (neutral-to-mildly-acid KAu(CN)2)
solutions.purpose: the standard high-performance selective gold: best coverage, adhesion, and color range; hardened (Co/Ni) variants for wear zones

composition.typical_range: 4-12 (as Au metal; pen solutions run richer than tank baths for speed, some concentrates to ~20)
composition.role: gold source; very stable Au(CN)2- complex tolerates open-air hand work
composition.hazard_class: acute toxic cyanide complex (H300/H310/H330 class); liberates HCN on contact with acid or below ~pH 3 [FACT]

composition.role: pH buffering (typ. mildly acid to neutral), conductivity for stable pen current

composition.chemical: hardener/color metal (Co or Ni salt) in 'hard gold' pen variants
composition.role: hardness (130-200 HV class) and shade control (Co warm, Ni pale)
composition.hazard_class: Co/Ni salts: sensitizers, Carc. class substances, aquatic toxic [FACT]

composition.role: film wetting on the nib, brightness, burn resistance

operating_window.temperature_C: room temperature 18-30 (pen solutions formulated for ambient; no heater) [FACT: published characteristic of pen/brush systems]
operating_window.pH: typically ~3.5-7 depending on formulation; NEVER acidified below ~3 [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium; exact per TDS]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: effective local CD high (brush regime tolerates 5-50x tank values) but the OPERATOR controls VOLTAGE, not CD
operating_window.voltage: 3-6 V typical jewelry pen setting [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high; TDS gives exact]
operating_window.agitation: IS the process — constant nib motion; stationary contact burns
operating_window.deposition_rate: flash (0.05-0.1 um) in 10-30 s of coverage; ~1-3 min per 0.1-0.2 um-class on a small zone; multi-pass with re-wetting for more [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
operating_window.anode: platinum / platinized titanium pen tip or pure graphite, insoluble

solutions.maintenance: Working aliquots deplete fast (small volume, rich drag-out on nib): track by color/coverage loss and either replenish per supplier concentrate or replace aliquot; never return used aliquot to stock. Keep dedicated nibs per solution. Contamination shows as dull/brown deposits — Fe from touching bare steel and Cu from clip jaws are the usual culprits. Store sealed, dark, cool; label with cyanide warning; absolute segregation from acids [FACT: HCN hazard].

solutions.purpose: safer-handling option for open hand-held DIY work; standard offer of jewelry pen-plating suppliers

composition.chemical: gold(I) sulfite complex (sodium or ammonium gold sulfite)
composition.role: gold source without cyanide; complex is less stable than cyanide — formulation carries excess sulfite
composition.hazard_class: lower acute toxicity than cyanide; sulfite releases SO2 on acidification; still a heavy-metal solution [FACT]

composition.role: stabilizes the Au(I) complex against disproportionation to gold dust

composition.chemical: buffer/conductivity salts + stabilizers (often EDTA-class, arsenite- or Tl-free grain refiners in modern decorative versions)

operating_window.voltage: 2-5 V typical pen setting [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium; TDS gives exact]
operating_window.deposition_rate: comparable flash rates to cyanide pens but narrower window; easier to burn/fog [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, low-medium]

solutions.maintenance: Sulfite gold is chemically the fragile one: solution slowly disproportionates (fine gold precipitate, brown tint) especially with light, heat, low sulfite, or acid drag-in — shelf life shorter than cyanide type; buy small bottles. An acid-activated surface must be rinsed well before the pen touches (acid kills the sulfite complex locally = staining). Filter or discard once turbid.

solutions.purpose: adhesion and barrier layer over steel/worn spots before gold; also the 'repair the repair' layer when a worn ring shows base metal

composition.chemical: nickel sulfamate or nickel sulfate (concentrated for brush regime)
composition.typical_range: brush solutions run metal-rich vs tank: ~75-140 as Ni salts (tens of g/L as Ni metal)
composition.role: nickel source; sulfamate version gives low-stress ductile deposit
composition.hazard_class: nickel salts: skin sensitizer (nickel allergy), Carc. class, aquatic toxic [FACT]

composition.chemical: chloride source + boric acid or proprietary buffer
composition.hazard_class: boric acid: Repr. class substance [FACT]; NiCl2 as above

operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: high local CD under moving swab
operating_window.voltage: 4-10 V class per TDS [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
operating_window.deposition_rate: brush Ni builds fast — visible white coverage in tens of seconds; ~1 um-class in a few minutes on a small zone [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]

solutions.maintenance: Dedicated nibs and cups (Ni cross-contamination ruins gold color). EN 1811 nickel-release rule still applies to the finished skin-contact piece even for repairs [FACT: regulation exists] — cover brush-Ni fully with gold of adequate thickness.

solutions.purpose: tankless pretreatment with the same handle: electro-clean then activate the exact zone to be plated

composition.chemical: acid activator (dilute sulfuric or proprietary acid salt)
composition.formula: H2SO4 ~5-10 vol% class or NaHSO4 solution
composition.role: strip oxide, activate Ni/steel for adhesion
composition.hazard_class: corrosive acid [FACT]; NEVER let activator contact cyanide gold solution or nibs [FACT: HCN]

operating_window.pH: cleaner strongly alkaline; activator strongly acid
operating_window.voltage: cleaner used at 6-12 V class, sometimes reverse polarity per TDS [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, low-medium]
operating_window.anode: graphite / stainless per kit (non-depositing steps only)

solutions.maintenance: Rinse pen zone thoroughly between EVERY solution; the whole failure economy of pen plating is cross-contamination on nibs and un-rinsed chemistry under the next layer.

prep_chain_required: 1. Degrease the work zone (solvent wipe or ultrasonic) — WHY: pen plating has no forgiving tank dwell; a fingerprint under a 0.1 um flash is instantly visible.
2. Electroclean the zone (pen electrocleaner or alkaline wipe + rinse) — WHY: water-break-free surface is the same non-negotiable as in tank work.
3. Activate: dilute acid for Ni/Cu surfaces; Wood's-type nickel strike (pen or dip) for stainless — WHY: passive oxide = zero adhesion; stainless's Cr2O3 film MUST be struck through [FACT].
4. Brush nickel undercoat where base steel is exposed or leveling/barrier is needed — WHY: gold direct on steel gives non-adherent immersion deposits and Fe contamination.
5. Rinse between every step, gold-recovery cup first after gold — WHY: cross-contamination and chemistry carry-under are the dominant pen-work failure causes.
ASSUMPTION: the piece is FINISHED and FORMED before pen work — brush plating is a last-operation/repair process by nature; it happily plates after forming, which is exactly its role in this vertical.

deposit_properties.purity_karat: fine-gold pens: 23.5-24k class (99+ % Au); hardened pens: 99.5% class with Co/Ni like tank hard gold; colored-gold pens (rose/green) deposit alloy shades at lower karat per TDS [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium]
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: soft gold pens 60-90 HV class; hardened pens 130-200 HV class — same metallurgy families as tank deposits [FACT: published typical ranges for the deposit types]
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: 0.05-0.5 um realistic per patient application session on a small zone; ~1-2 um achievable with multi-pass + Ah counting but uniformity degrades; industrial brush Ni/Cu builds 10s-100s um but that is machine-part repair, not decorative gold [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, high]
deposit_properties.color_control: the WEAK point: shade depends on operator speed, pressure, voltage, nib wetness, and solution age simultaneously — matching a pen-plated repair spot to a tank-plated field is a skilled operation; always test on a hidden area first, keep a retained color standard, and expect visible patch boundaries at flash thickness on large smooth surfaces
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: PLATE-THEN-FORM ANSWER FOR THIS FAMILY: moot in the production sense — brush plating is applied AFTER forming by definition, which is precisely why it belongs in this vertical: it is the corrective for the plate-then-form problem (form the wire, tank-plate, then brush-repair bend-damage or plate zones the rack contact shadowed). The deposits themselves have the same ductility as their tank cousins (hardened gold brittle <1% elongation class, soft gold ductile), so do not form AFTER brush plating either.

testing_acceptance.test: coating thickness by XRF on the plated zone
testing_acceptance.acceptance: meets whatever class is claimed for the ZONE; brush flash must not be sold under full micron-plating claims

testing_acceptance.test: adhesion — tape test and burnish on same-sequence coupon
testing_acceptance.standard_class: ASTM B571 class (tape, burnish); AMS 2451 is the aerospace brush-plating quality class [FACT: standard exists]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no lift/peel; burnish does not smear-through to undercoat

testing_acceptance.test: color match of repair vs surrounding field
testing_acceptance.standard_class: visual vs retained standard under D65-class daylight lamp; NIHS 1N-3N shade naming
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no visible patch boundary at arm's length under daylight lamp (define in-house)

testing_acceptance.standard_class: in-house wipe/pH check of rinsed piece
testing_acceptance.acceptance: neutral, no dried electrolyte films on a wearable item

testing_acceptance.test: nickel release if brush Ni was used on skin-contact zone
testing_acceptance.standard_class: EN 1811 / EN 12472 (EU REACH Annex XVII e.27) [FACT: regulation]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: below 0.5 ug/cm2/week class limit after simulated wear

testing_acceptance.standard_class: magnifier inspection 10x; salt-droplet class spot test on coupon
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no base-metal exposure in the repaired zone

defects_and_remedies.cause: nib too dry, stopped motion, voltage too high for the solution
defects_and_remedies.remedy: re-wet every few seconds, keep constant overlapping strokes, drop 1-2 V; burned spots must be stripped/re-prepped, not plated over
verify work = negative before every session; label leads permanently

defects_and_remedies.cause: grease/fingerprint under deposit, passive nickel (waited too long after activation), gold direct on steel
defects_and_remedies.remedy: enforce glove handling post-clean, re-activate if >1-2 min delay, always brush-Ni over exposed steel first

defects_and_remedies.defect: visible patch boundary / color mismatch vs rest of piece
defects_and_remedies.cause: different chemistry-shade than original plate, flash too thin over different-colored undercoat, operator speed/voltage drift
defects_and_remedies.remedy: test-match on hidden area, feather edges with light fast strokes, extend the plated zone to a natural design boundary (groove, edge)

defects_and_remedies.defect: dull, hazy, or brown deposit from a solution that worked yesterday
defects_and_remedies.cause: working aliquot depleted or contaminated (Fe from steel touch, Cu from clip, Ni cross-over from shared nib)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: discard aliquot (into gold-recovery bottle), fresh aliquot, dedicated nibs per chemistry, insulate/relocate clip

defects_and_remedies.cause: electrolyte residue not rinsed off, hard-water final rinse
defects_and_remedies.remedy: immediate rinse (recovery cup first), DI final rinse, warm-air dry

defects_and_remedies.defect: sulfite gold solution turns turbid/brown with gold dust
defects_and_remedies.cause: disproportionation: age, light, heat, acid drag-in, low free sulfite
defects_and_remedies.remedy: buy small bottles, store cool/dark, rinse acid off work before pen contact, replace when turbid (send residue to gold recovery)

defects_and_remedies.defect: unplated shadow at the cathode clip
defects_and_remedies.cause: clip blocks its own contact spot
defects_and_remedies.remedy: plan clip placement on hidden feature; plate in two sessions moving the clip; or use back-side probe contact

cost_drivers: gold solution price per gram Au contained — pen bottles carry a heavy packaging/formulation premium over bulk salt (often 2-4x per Au gram vs tank replenisher class) [ESTIMATE: market pattern, medium]
solution wastage: nib drag-out and discarded aliquots are a much larger FRACTION of gold used than tank drag-out — recovery cup discipline is the lever
operator time: minutes per zone, fully manual, non-parallel — this is why brush is repair/accent economics, not production economics
platinum pen tips and nib consumables (cheap individually, recurring)
rework rate driven by operator skill curve (burns and mismatches early on)
essentially zero capital: PSU + pens + bottles ≈ the cheapest entry ticket of ALL gold processes in this vertical

hazards: cyanide-type gold pen solutions are acute toxics handled OPEN and hand-held — skin/eye contact and acid-contact HCN generation are the top risks [FACT]
acid activator + cyanide solution on the same bench = HCN gas potential [FACT]
nickel solutions: skin sensitizer (nickel allergy) and Carc.-class salts [FACT]
sulfite solutions release SO2 on acidification [FACT]
low-voltage DC itself is not a shock hazard at pen settings, but shorted nib-to-work sparking can splash solution
controls: nitrile gloves + safety glasses ALWAYS; work over a spill tray
physical segregation: acids on one side, cyanide bottles on the other, never share cups/nibs/pipettes
prefer the cyanide-free sulfite pen for DIY start; graduate to cyanide-type only with handling discipline in place
small working aliquots only; stock bottles stay closed and stored locked, labeled, away from acids
ventilation: extractor fan or strong airflow at the bench
written spill + first-aid card at the bench (cyanide first-aid is time-critical) [FACT]
safety.waste: All rinses and dead aliquots into labeled recovery bottles (gold value + heavy-metal compliance); never drain-dump cyanide, nickel, or gold-bearing liquids [FACT: regulated waste classes]; volumes are tiny (ml-scale), so accumulate and send to a precious-metal refiner / licensed waste route — the refiner route usually PAYS for gold-bearing waste.

diy_feasibility.verdict: HIGHEST DIY feasibility of every gold process in this vertical — this is the recommended FIRST HANDS-ON process for the owner: sub-$300-class entry, room temperature, ml-scale chemistry, immediate visible results, and it teaches the whole prep-adhesion-color discipline that tank plating then scales up. BUT it is a repair/accent/learning tool, not the production route for whole steel-wire pieces — pair it with tank electroplating (production) as the intended end-state.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: bench CC/CV power supply (0-30 V) or commercial pen-plating station; platinum-tip pen (or graphite rod + cotton) with spare nibs; 30-100 ml each of: pen electrocleaner, activator, brush nickel, and ONE gold pen solution (start cyanide-free sulfite); alligator-clip cathode lead; beakers, spill tray, gloves, glasses, recovery bottle; a box of steel/brass coupons to burn through while learning. [ESTIMATE: setup class, high confidence on composition of the kit]
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: cannot economically plate whole pieces in quantity (operator-minutes per piece); thickness claims above ~1 um-class are impractical/dishonest for brush-only work; color matching to tank-plated fields is a skill ceiling; non-conductive substrates still excluded without seed metallization; cyanide-type solutions demand handling discipline no matter how small the bottle.
